newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey host to fat rights convention.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey host to fat rights convention.

text.p: The 400 conventioneers checking in Tuesday at the Cherry Hill Hilton are some of the hotel's biggest customers.

The annual convention of the National Association to Advance Fat Acceptance will be meeting through Sunday, holding seminars, fashion shows and in general to fight for the concept that people should not be discriminated against because of their weight.
Its advocacy goes beyond quashing fat jokes. Members do not blush at being called fat.
"We've taken back the word 'fat' the way the gay community has taken back the word 'queer,'" said Sally Smith of Pasadena, California, executive director of NAAFA.
The organisation, founded in 1969, embraces education. A convention session will dispute the common medical statement that being overweight endangers health.
Another morale builder: A fashion show Thursday.
The convention also will attract a flock of merchants with products geared to the large customer -- oversized furniture and extra-large clothing, among others.
"Our message is that everyone, regardless of size, has the right to a life of dignity and respect," said Bob Sponagle, president of the host chapter.
